value.manufacture_protocol:
see manufacturer's web site
The U133 set includes 2 arrays with a total of 44928 entries and was indexed 29-Jan-2002.
The set includes over 1,000,000 unique oligonucleotide features covering more than 39,000 transcript variants, which in turn represent greater than 33,000 of the best characterized human genes.
Sequences were selected from GenBank, dbEST, and RefSeq. Sequence clusters were created from Build 133 of UniGene (April 20, 2001) and refined by analysis and comparison with a number of other publicly available databases including the Washington University EST trace repository and the University of California, Santa Cruz golden-path human genome database (April 2001 release). In addition, ESTs were analyzed for untrimmed low-quality sequence information, correct orientation, false priming, false clustering, alternative splicing and alternative polyadenylation.

post.description: Start here to find GEO accessions for a disease, gene, tissue, organism, assay or platform; then call `series` for the design, samples and files of a GSE, `sample` for one GSM's characteristics and protocols, or `platform` for a GPL.

dataset_type.description: Experiment type exactly as GEO names it, e.g. `Expression profiling by array`, `Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing`, `Methylation profiling by high throughput sequencing`, `Genome binding/occupancy profiling by high throughput sequencing`.

entry_type.description:
Record type: `GSE` series (default), `GDS` curated DataSets, `GPL` platforms, `GSM` samples, or `all`.

Provider reference: allowed values ["GSE", "GDS", "GPL", "GSM", "all"]; default "GSE".

limit.description:
Results per page.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 50; default 20.

max_date.description: Latest release (public) date, same forms as `min_date`. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}(/[0-9]{2}(/[0-9]{2})?)?$.

offset.description:
Zero-based index of the first result.

Provider reference: minimum 0; maximum 1000000; default 0.

organism.description: Organism, scientific or common name (`Homo sapiens`, `mouse`); includes sub-taxa.

platform.description: Platform accession (`GPL570`); restricts results to records using that platform. Pattern: ^\s*[Gg][Pp][Ll][0-9]{1,9}\s*$.

query.description: Entrez query over GEO DataSets: free text or field-tagged terms such as `brca1[Gene Name]`, `liver[Title]`, `smith j[Author]`, with AND/OR/NOT. Optional when a filter is given.

200.description:
Search GEO DataSets (NCBI E-utilities esearch + esummary, db=gds) with Entrez query syntax plus filters for record type (`GSE` series by default, `GDS`, `GPL`, `GSM` or `all`), organism, experiment type, platform and release-date range. Returns the total count, the Entrez translation of the term and one summary per hit (accession, title, summary, organisms, experiment types, platforms, sample count, release date, PubMed ids, supplementary file types, BioProject, file directory). Offset-paginated; an empty result is a valid empty page.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `results` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accession` | string | GEO accession (`GSE…`, `GDS…`, `GPL…` or `GSM…`). |
| `bioproject` | string | BioProject accession. |
| `datasets` | string[] | Curated DataSet accessions (`GDS…`) derived from or using this record. |
| `entry_type` | string | Record type: `GSE` (series), `GDS` (curated DataSet), `GPL` (platform) or `GSM` (sample). |
| `ftp_url` | string | Directory of the record's files on NCBI's file server (https). |
| `organisms` | string[] | Organism names. |
| `platforms` | string[] | Platform accessions (`GPL…`) used. |
| `public_date` | string | Date the record became public (`YYYY-MM-DD`); null when GEO gives none. |
| `pubmed_ids` | string[] | Linked PubMed ids. |
| `sample_count` | number | Number of samples; null for samples. |
| `series` | string[] | Related series accessions (`GSE…`), at most 50; for a platform these are series that used it. Search with `platform` for the full list. |
| `series_count` | number | Number of related series before the 50-item cap. |
| `summary` | string | Summary text; for a sample its source; null when empty. |
| `supplementary_file_types` | string[] | Supplementary file formats, e.g. `CEL`, `TSV`. |
| `title` | string |  |
| `types` | string[] | Experiment types, e.g. `Expression profiling by array`; empty for samples and platforms. |
| `uid` | string | Entrez GEO DataSets uid. |
| `url` | string | GEO accession viewer page for the record: `https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc={accession}`. Cite it when reusing the record. |

results.summary: The mission of expO is to build on the technologies and outcomes of the Human Genome Project to accelerate improved clinical management of cancer patients.  IGC's Expression Project for Oncology (expO) seeks to integrate longitudinal clinical annotation with gene expression data for a unique and powerful portrait of human malignancies, providing critical perspective on diagnostic markers, prognostic indicators, and therapeutic targets.  The goal of expO and its consortium supporters is to procure tissue samples under standard conditions and perform gene expression analyses on a clinically annotated set of deidentified tumor samples. The tumor data is updated with clinical outcomes and is released into the public domain without intellectual property restriction.  Series-matrices are available at ftp://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/geo/DATA/SeriesMatrix/GSE2109/.  For more information, see http://www.intgen.org/ Keywords: cancer portraits

Provider reference: minimum 0; maximum 5000; default 500.

url.description: GEO accession viewer URL, e.g. `https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE2034`. Exactly one of `accession` and `url`.

200.description:
One GEO series (GSE) from the GEO accession viewer's SOFT text, with sample titles from E-utilities esummary: title, summary, overall design, experiment types, release/submission/last-update dates, contributors and contact (name, institute, country), platforms, organisms with taxonomy ids, sample count and sample list (accession and title), linked PubMed ids, supplementary file URLs, related BioProject/SRA/SuperSeries records and the file directory. Unknown and still-private accessions are `not_found`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accession` | string | GEO accession. |
| `contact` | object | Submitting contact as GEO publishes it (name, institute and country only; email, phone and street address are not returned). |
| `contributors` | string[] | Contributors in GEO order. |
| `ftp_url` | string | The series directory on NCBI's file server (https), which also holds the series matrix and SOFT/MINiML family files. |
| `last_update_date` | string | Last update date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). |
| `observed_at_ms` | number | Unix milliseconds when the program observed the source. |
| `organisms` | object[] | Organisms with NCBI Taxonomy ids, in GEO order. |
| `overall_design` | string | Overall design; null when the submitter gave none. |
| `platforms` | string[] | Platform accessions (`GPL…`). |
| `public_date` | string | Date the record became public, from `status` (`YYYY-MM-DD`); null when GEO gives none. |
| `pubmed_ids` | string[] | Linked PubMed ids; empty when unpublished. |
| `relations` | object[] | Links to related GEO, BioProject, BioSample and SRA records. |
| `sample_count` | number | Number of samples in the series. |
| `samples` | object[] | Samples in GEO order, at most `sample_limit`. |
| `samples_truncated` | boolean | True when `sample_count` exceeds `sample_limit`. |
| `status` | string | GEO status line, e.g. `Public on Feb 23 2005`. |
| `submission_date` | string | Submission date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). |
| `summary` | string | Series summary; lines joined with newlines. |
| `supplementary_files` | string[] | Supplementary file URLs on NCBI's file server (`ftp://` rewritten to the equivalent `https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/`), in GEO order; empty when none. |
| `terms_url` | string | GEO data-use statement (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/info/disclaimer.html): NCBI places no restrictions on GEO data, but submitters may assert patent, copyright or other rights in what they deposited. |
| `title` | string |  |
| `types` | string[] | Experiment types, e.g. `Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing`. |
| `url` | string | GEO accession viewer page for the record: `https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc={accession}`. Cite it when reusing the record. |
